rationale: Both rewrite the character-by-character parser as a clean line-by-line one with a headerLevel helper and an applyEmphasis helper. A keeps its state local and manages it through two small closures, flushParagraph and closeList. It buffers paragraph text separately and writes each <li> as a complete element, so every construct is handled in exactly one place. B moves the close helpers to package level, but they take `*strings.Builder` and `*bool` arguments, which is clumsy and less idiomatic than closures or a small struct. B also opens <li> on one line and closes it on the next item or in closeList, which spreads the list markup across places and is harder to follow. B's per-line emphasis is arguably better Markdown behaviour. But in a refactoring exercise, A's documented choice to keep the original whole-document semantics is defensible, and its overall structure is cleaner and easier to maintain.
